Transcribe every complete printed text line exactly, one array element per printed line, top to bottom. Preserve spelling, capitalisation, punctuation, printed abbreviations, section marks and end-of-line hyphenation. Hebrew, Aramaic, Arabic, Syriac, Greek and Ethiopic must be Unicode text with every visible vowel point, dagesh, shin or sin dot, accent and diacritic, and with no point that is not printed; write them in logical order with no bidi control characters, keep the words of a right-to-left phrase in the order they are read, and keep the printed left-to-right order of separate items in a list. Transcribe the letters actually printed even when they are not the dictionary spelling: never insert or drop a vav or yod, and never replace a form with a more familiar one. Distinguish Arabic from Syriac by the letter shapes. If a line is only partially visible at the top or bottom edge, omit it entirely rather than guessing. Never add, reorder, translate, normalise or omit anything that is fully visible. If the crop contains no text, return an empty array.

Note. Instead of the sing. אַחַר, the
plur. אַחֲרֵי is far more frequently used;
see below. With suffixes the plur. form
is always used.
Plur. אֲחָרִים, only in constr. אַחֲרֵי, c.
suff. אַחֲרַי, אַחֲרֵיכֶם, אַחֲרֵיהֶם, etc.
1. Subst. the hinder parts, 2 Sam. 2,
23 בְּאַחֲרֵי הַחֲנִית with the hinder end of
the spear.
2. Prep. a) Of place, behind, Judg.
18, 12 where it is i. q. on the west of, see
in אָחוֹר no. 2. More freq. after, behind
any one, Lev. 26, 33. 1 Sam. 14, 37.
2 K. 19, 21. (אֲשֶׁר) אַחֲרֵיהֶם those who

lines.note: Only the order differs. Printed visual order left→right is אַחֲרֵיהֶם then (אֲשֶׁר); as one RTL run the rightmost (אֲשֶׁר) is logically first, giving Reading A's order (אֲשֶׁר) אַחֲרֵיהֶם. Reading B puts the parenthesis logically second, which would render visually reversed. All vowel points, shin dot and the yod in אַחֲרֵיהֶם are as both readings have them.

lines.text: go after them, their flatterers, parasites,
Ps. 49, 14. Hence, with verbs of going,
to follow; also הָיָה אַחֲרֵי פ׳ to be after,
to go after any one, i. q. to follow, to be
on one's side, Ex. 23, 2. 2 Sam. 2, 10.
Comp. 1 K. 1, 7. Prov. 28, 23 מוֹכִיחַ אָדָם
אַחֲרַי חֵן יִמְצָא he that rebuketh a man
after me (i. e. after my precepts) shall
find favour. b) Of time, after, Gen.
16, 13. 17, 8. With inf. after that, after,
3. Conj. אַחֲרֵי אֲשֶׁר after that, Deut.
24, 4. Josh. 9, 16. 23, 1; rarely with אֲשֶׁר
omitted, Lev. 25, 48. Once אַחֲרֵי כַּאֲשֶׁר
Josh. 2, 7.
4. אַחֲרֵי־כֵן pr. after so, after it had so
happened, i. e. afterwards, Gen. 6, 4.
ܒܳܬܰܪܟܶܢ and ܒܳܬܰܪ ܗܳܟܰܢ. With אֲשֶׁר added
it becomes a conjunction, i. q. אַחֲרֵי אֲשֶׁר
after that, like Lat. posteaquam for post-
quam, Deut. 24, 4. 2 Sam. 24, 10. In the
later Hebrew we find also אַחֲרֵי זֹאת
after this, afterwards, Job 42, 16. Ezra
9, 10. Comp. Chald. אַחֲרֵי דְנָה Dan. 2,
5. With other prepositions:
a) מֵאַחֲרֵי, once מִן אַחֲרֵי 1 Chr. 17, 7,
pr. from after, from behind, from going
or following after; chiefly used of those
who abandon a person or party whom
they have before followed, Num. 14, 43.
Deut. 7, 4. 2 Sam. 20, 2. Also at or on
the back, behind, after, (comp. מִן no. 3.
Of time, after, Ecc. 10, 14; and in Neh.
4, 7 מֵאַחֲרֵי לְ, in the same sense. Hence
מֵאַחֲרֵי כֵן pr. after so, i. e. afterwards,
b) אֶל־אַחֲרֵי after, with verbs of mo-
tion. 2 K. 9, 18 סֹב אֶל־אַחֲרַי turn thee
after me, behind me, 2 Sam. 5, 23.
c) עַל־אַחֲרֵי i. q. אַחֲרֵי, Ez. 41, 15.
Comp. עַל no. 3. b.
אַחַר Chald. plur. constr. אַחֲרֵי, after,
Dan. 2, 29; but by Hebraism. The
pure Chaldee preposit. is בָּתַר.
אַחֲרוֹן, fem. אַחֲרֹנָה, from אַחַר with
the adj. ending וֹן.
